page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz, supporting hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 0.9 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud infrastructure. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1086.39, while the multi-core score is 1408.88. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers at 13.22 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.3 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are limited, as shown by a passmark CPU encryption score of 652.65 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.91 GB/sec.

Due to its low memory allocation of 2.0 GB and lack of local storage, the n1-highcpu-2 is highly constrained for memory-intensive applications or large-scale database operations, as reflected in its low passmark database score of 451.25. However, because it offers dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources, it provides predictable execution for lightweight, compute-bound utility tasks. It is best suited for basic web serving, simple background workers, lightweight automation scripts, or small-scale batch processing where memory requirements are minimal.
